name: Anglophone Crisis (Ambazonia separatist conflict), Cameroon
started: 2017-10-01 (Ambazonian declaration of independence; conflict began after 2016 protests)
summary: Separatists in Cameroon's English-speaking Northwest and Southwest regions have fought the state since 2017, now as a fragmented, low-level guerrilla war of ambushes, IEDs, kidnappings for ransom and army raids that kill fighters and civilians alike. Fighting continued through the October 2025 election and into 2026, interrupted only by a three-day ceasefire for Pope Leo XIV's April 2026 visit to Bamenda. It matters because it has displaced hundreds of thousands and has no peace process.

sides.name: Government of Cameroon
members: Cameroon Armed Forces incl. Rapid Intervention Brigade (BIR)
sides.strength: Older infobox estimate: 12,500 troops and 9,000 militia (Wikipedia, 2019 data).

sides.name: Ambazonian separatists
members: Ambazonia Defence Forces (armed wing of the Ambazonia Governing Council)
Interim Government of Ambazonia and its forces
Local militias such as Bui Unity Warriors, Donga Mantung Unity Warriors, Unity Warriors of Fako, Ambazonia State Army
backers: Diaspora fundraising (ADF commanders Benedict Nwana Kuah and Pascal Kikishy Wongbi arrested in Minnesota in Sept 2025)
leaders: Sisiku Julius Ayuk Tabe (jailed 'Nera 10' leader; life sentence annulled March 2026, retrial ordered)
sides.strength: Older estimate 2,000-4,000 fighters (Wikipedia, May 2019); no current figure.

background: The crisis began with lawyers' and teachers' protests in 2016 against the marginalisation of the Anglophone minority, which the government met with force. Separatists declared the independent state of 'Ambazonia' on 1 October 2017 and took up arms. Swiss-mediated talks in 2019 failed, as did the government's 2019 'Major National Dialogue'.

The movement has fractured into many local militias and rival diaspora leaderships, and the war has become partly criminal (kidnapping for ransom). Why it matters: there is no credible negotiating partner on either side, and civilians are squeezed by separatist lockdowns and by army raids.
year: Separatists (the Ambazonia Governing Council and Ayaba Cho Lucas) declared a week-long lockdown from 6-12 Oct 2025 around the presidential election; Anglophone towns were largely deserted on 12 Oct. Attacks followed: a livestock ministry official was shot dead in Bamenda (28 Oct), four gendarmes were killed in an ambush in Tubah/Bambili (5 Nov), suspected separatists killed four worshippers at a mosque in Sabga (13 Nov), and IEDs killed soldiers in Bamenda (30 Nov) and Bangshie (17 Dec). Army raids in Bafut killed nine people including four civilians (5 Dec 2025) and a commander, 'General Jakaban' (14 Mar 2026). Gunmen killed at least 15 at Gidado, Ndu (14 Jan 2026). On 19 Mar 2026 the Supreme Court annulled the life sentences of the 'Nera 10' leaders and ordered a retrial. A separatist alliance declared a ceasefire for 15-17 April for Pope Leo XIV's visit to Bamenda; fighting resumed afterwards, and an army raid at Ndzerem-Nyam, Jakiri killed at least 14 fighters and 6 civilians (26 Apr). Ambushes and shootings continued in Belo, Bambui and Noni into June 2026.
situation: As of late October 2026 the conflict is a grinding low-intensity guerrilla war concentrated in Mezam (Bamenda, Bafut, Tubah), Bui, Boyo and Donga-Mantung in the Northwest, and Fako and Meme in the Southwest. Kidnappings for ransom, IEDs and small ambushes are the main separatist tools; army raids on hideouts often kill civilians. No negotiations are under way; the Nera 10 retrial is the one notable legal development.
technical: Separatists rely heavily on IEDs, including against soldiers in Bamenda (30 Nov 2025), Bangshie (17 Dec 2025) and Mile 6 Nkwen (28 Dec 2025) (Wikipedia timelines).
'Ghost town' lockdowns are a political weapon: a strict one-week lockdown was imposed for 6-12 Oct 2025 around the presidential vote.
Kidnapping for ransom is routine: a CPDM MP (Oct 2025), a journalist (Dec 2025), students in Bambili (Dec 2025), about 12 bus passengers at Sabga (June 2026).
Army raids on hideouts are lethal for civilians: Bafut (5 Dec 2025, 5 fighters and 4 civilians killed), Ndzerem-Nyam (26 Apr 2026, 14 fighters and 6 civilians killed, 38 motorcycles burned).
Command decapitation: 'General Jakaban' killed in Bafut on 14 Mar 2026.
Diaspora finance: two ADF commanders were arrested in Minnesota on 5 Sept 2025 and charged in the US.
The April 2026 papal ceasefire (15-17 April) was the first coordinated separatist truce noted in the sources, and broke down within days.
casualties: No 12-month total found. Incident-level deaths in the Wikipedia timelines for Oct 2025 to June 2026 total several dozen to over 100, and these lists are incomplete. Intensity 'medium' is an estimate. Long-run: thousands killed since 2017 (International Crisis Group, as cited by Wikipedia).
displaced: More than half a million people forced from their homes (International Crisis Group, 2019, cited by Wikipedia); no current figure retrieved. NRC has ranked Cameroon's displacement crisis among the world's most neglected.

timeline.event: Separatists impose a one-week lockdown around the presidential election.
Four gendarmes killed in an ambush in Tubah.
Four worshippers killed at a mosque in Sabga.
Army raid in Bafut kills five fighters and four civilians; two soldiers killed in Fundong.
At least 15 killed by gunmen at Gidado, Ndu.
Supreme Court annuls Nera 10 life sentences and orders a retrial.
Three-day separatist ceasefire for Pope Leo XIV's visit to Bamenda.
Army raid at Ndzerem-Nyam, Jakiri kills 14 fighters and 6 civilians.
Two soldiers and two civilians shot dead at a bar in Noni, Bui.

outlook: Watch the Nera 10 retrial, whether the papal truce precedent leads to any talks, separatist lockdowns around the legislative elections postponed to 20 Dec 2026, and continued kidnapping-for-ransom.

zones.name: Mezam (Bamenda, Bafut, Tubah, Bambili)
zones.note: Most frequent IED attacks, kidnappings and army raids.

zones.name: Bui, Ndu and Donga-Mantung
zones.note: Jakiri raid (Apr 2026), Noni bar shooting (Jun 2026), Gidado massacre at Ndu (Jan 2026).

zones.name: Boyo and Belo (Fundong)
zones.note: Ambushes on soldiers in Belo (Mar and Jun 2026) and Fundong (Dec 2025).

zones.name: Southwest (Fako, Meme, Muyuka)
zones.note: Separatist attack at Ikata, Muyuka (Mar 2026); Unity Warriors of Fako.

battles.name: Army raid at Ndzerem-Nyam, Jakiri

battles.losses: At least 14 separatist fighters and 6 civilians killed; 38 motorcycles burned (Wikipedia timeline).
battles.significance: Deadliest single event in the conflict found for the window; came days after the papal ceasefire ended.
